title: Working at Redwood: Roles, Career Ladders, Benefits, Hiring & Onboarding, and Internal Tools
author: Priya Singh
content:
Summary

This page consolidates Redwood's core employee-facing policies and practical guides for: working at Redwood, role definitions and career ladders, benefits & perks, hiring and onboarding, and the primary internal tools new and existing employees rely on. The goal is to provide a single, up-to-date reference for new hires, hiring managers, and people managers.

1) Working at Redwood — culture, expectations, and logistics

Intro
Redwood is an engineering-first company that values ownership, reliability, and the practical pursuit of product-market fit. We emphasize pragmatic decision-making, high-quality engineering, and customer empathy. The sections below summarize day-to-day expectations, working models, and how we support hybrid/remote collaboration.

Core values (short list)
- Build for production: prioritize reliability, observability, and reproducibility.
- Default to ownership: own the outcome, not just the ticket.
- Customer-first engineering: measure decisions by customer impact.
- Respectful, candid communication: clear feedback, with empathy.

Working model and hours
- Standard core hours: 10:00–16:00 local time for team collaboration.
- Flexible schedule outside core hours. Individual teams may set stricter core windows for global coordination.
- Redwood supports distributed work. Engineers may be remote or hybrid; on-site days are coordinated by teams for planning, retros, and key workshops.

Time off, leaves, and holidays (summary)
- PTO: 25 days annual accrual for full-time employees, prorated at start/end of employment.
- Parental leave: up to 18 weeks primary caregiver paid leave, plus 6 weeks for secondary caregivers (policy summary; see People Ops for full terms).
- Sick leave: 10 days per year, separate from PTO.
- Public holidays: company observes 10 US/regionally adjusted holidays.

Inclusion & accessibility
- Reasonable accommodations and accessibility support are available; contact people-ops@redwood.com.
- We run inclusive hiring and behavioral interviewing trainings for interviewers; schedule through L&D.

2) Roles and career ladders — structure and promotion process

Overview
Redwood maintains clear individual contributor (IC) and manager career ladders across core functions: Engineering, Product, Research (Applied ML), SRE, and Developer Experience. Role titles are intentionally consistent to make cross-team moves and leveling transparent.

Canonical levels (engineering-focused)
- IC1 / Associate Engineer (entry-level)
- IC2 / Engineer
- IC3 / Senior Engineer
- IC4 / Staff Engineer
- IC5 / Principal Engineer

Manager track
- M1 / Engineering Manager (small team)
- M2 / Senior Engineering Manager
- M3 / Director of Engineering

Expectations by level (summary table)
Title | Scope & impact | Typical tenure
---|---|---
IC2 — Engineer | Delivers features with minimal guidance; owns small-to-medium components | 1–3 years
IC3 — Senior Engineer | Leads technical design; mentors others; owns cross-team projects | 3–6 years
IC4 — Staff Engineer | Drives architecture decisions; measurable org-level impact | 5+ years

Promotion and leveling process (step-by-step)
1. Candidate (engineer or manager) and manager discuss readiness and set a promotion rubric and timeline (1–3 months typical).
2. Manager submits a leveling packet (summary of signals + examples) to People Ops using the promotion template.
3. Panel review: cross-functional reviewers evaluate impact, scope, and competencies.
4. Calibration and decision: final determination and new comp/level communicated.
5. If promoted, update career plan and objectives; if not, receive written feedback and a 3–6 month development plan.

Career development and learning
- Annual career check-ins with manager + optional 1:1 with People Ops.
- Learning stipend: $1,500/year for role-relevant courses, conferences, or books. Pre-approval required for conferences > $500.

3) Benefits & perks — summary and how to access

Health & financial benefits
- Medical, dental, and vision: multiple plan tiers; full-time employees receive employer contribution to premiums.
- 401(k) / retirement plan with company match for US employees; local equivalents in other geographies.
- Equity: annual grants for new hires and refresh grants for tenured employees per compensation cycle.

Pay & compensation cadence
- Salary bands updated annually. Compensation reviews: performance-based increases during mid-year and end-of-year cycles.
- Bonus & equity refresh guidelines in Compensation docs (People Ops).

Perks and wellbeing
- Wellness stipend: $200/year for mental health, fitness, or wellbeing services.
- Home office allowance: $800 one-time for new hires to set up an ergonomic workspace.
- Commuter benefits: for employees in regions with commuter programs, pre-tax options available.

Family-friendly policies
- Parental coaching and return-to-work planning.
- Backup child/elder care benefit accessible through the benefits portal.

How to enroll or ask questions
- Open enrollment: People Ops sends an annual schedule and step-by-step enrollment guide.
- For benefits questions: benefits@redwood.com (include employee ID).

4) Hiring and onboarding overview — how we hire and how we welcome new hires

Hiring philosophy
- Hiring decisions balance technical skill, cultural fit, and potential for impact. We apply structured interviews (rubrics) to minimize bias and maximize predictability.

Interview stages (standard for engineering roles)
1. Recruiter screen (30–45 minutes): role fit, compensation expectations, high-level background.
2. Technical screen or take-home exercise (45–90 minutes) depending on level.
3. On-site loop (virtual or in-person): 4–6 interviews covering coding, system design (level-dependent), ownership/behavioral, and role-specific deep dive.
4. Hiring committee calibration and final decision.

Offer and background checks
- Offers approved by Hiring Manager, Recruiting Lead, and People Ops.
- Reference checks and background checks are completed for all offers contingent on local regulations.

Onboarding timeline (first 90 days)
Day 0–1: Preboarding
- HR sends welcome packet, equipment survey, and access instructions (Okta invite, Slack, email).
- Hardware shipped per equipment form.

Week 1: Orientation
- People Ops orientation: benefits overview, payroll setup, and policies.
- Team orientation: manager 1:1 to set initial goals and required reading.
- Tech onboarding: access to GitHub, CI, internal Confluence pages, and the dev env bootstrapping guide.

First 30 days: contribution ramp
- Complete mandatory trainings (security, privacy, and compliance).
- Ship a small ticket or documentation change to familiarize with codebase and processes.

60–90 days: impact and reflection
- Complete a 60-day sync with manager to assess ramp, blockers, and development plan.
- Formal 90-day review to confirm expectations and next goals.

New hire checklist (condensed)
- Hardware received and tested.
- Okta access and MFA configured.
- Slack joined + team channels followed.
- GitHub access granted; developer access checklist completed.
- Completed security and privacy trainings.

5) Internal tools guide — quick reference and owners

Overview: primary systems
- Slack (communication) — primary for async chat and #team channels.
- Confluence (documentation) — canonical company documentation and playbooks.
- GitHub (source control) — all prod code, PRs, and code reviews.
- Jira / Linear (tickets) — team-level and cross-team work tracking. Teams choose between Jira or Linear; see team wiki for team preference.
- Okta (SSO) — single sign-on for cloud apps. MFA is required for all employees.
- CI/CD (Buildkite / GitHub Actions) — pipelines, release tags, and deploy runbooks.
- VPN & VPC access — for private deployments and internal-only consoles. Request via infra-access@redwood.com.

Onboarding steps for tools (commands & examples)
1. Okta / SSO: Accept invite, set up MFA (authenticator app preferred).
2. Slack: Join #all, #eng, #people-ops, and your product/team channels. Pin important team docs in channel.
3. GitHub: Accept organization invite; set up SSH key and add to profile. Example commands:
   - ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -C "your_email@example.com"
   - eval "$(ssh-agent -s)"
   - ssh-add ~/.ssh/id_ed25519
4. Local dev environment: follow team-specific README in <repo-root>/docs/LOCAL_DEV.md. Typical steps:
   - git clone git@github.com:redwood/repo.git
   - make deps && make start-dev

Access requests and support
- Access request flow: fill out the Access Request form (linked in People Ops onboarding packet). Tags: include owner_team and justification. Approvals routed to owners automatically.
- Support contacts: infra-access@redwood.com, people-ops@redwood.com, security@redwood.com.

Tool owners and contacts (table)
Owner | System | Contact
---|---|---
Platform & Infra | VPN, VPC, CI/CD | infra-access@redwood.com
People Ops | Okta, benefits, onboarding | people-ops@redwood.com
Security | MFA, SSO policies, vulnerability reporting | security@redwood.com
Dev Productivity | GitHub, Buildkite, repos | dev-prod@redwood.com

6) Running effective onboarding programs — for hiring managers

Manager checklist (pre-start)
1. Prepare a 30/60/90 day plan and first-week schedule.
2. Ensure work tickets ready and meaningful for Day 1–14.
3. Book recurring 1:1s and relevant onboarding sessions.
4. Add new hire to team channels and calendars.

First 7 days (manager actions)
1. Daily check-ins during week 1.
2. Pair programming sessions and codebase walkthroughs.
3. Assign a peer buddy for culture and navigation questions.

Ongoing: feedback and leveling coaching
- Run explicit calibration conversations before promotion cycles.
- Provide written feedback and examples to support promotion packets.
